newsitem.title: USA: Stocks little changed, bonds up before Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Stocks little changed, bonds up before Fed meeting.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks edged lower Monday as investors awaited the Federal Reserve's meeting on interest rates starting Tuesday, while bonds rose after fresh economic reports pointed to steady growth with little inflation.
The dollar rose. Oil ended little changed.

The Dow Jones industrial average fell 6.93 points to 6,806.16. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,388 to 1,107 on moderate volume of 463 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"It's like hurry-up-and-wait time," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital.
Most economists believe policy-makers at the Fed, the nation's central bank, will vote to hold short-term rates steady at the meeting, which ends on Wednesday.

But even so investors seemed content to await the outcome of the meeting, and some analysts said stocks may remain in a holding pattern until Friday, when the critical monthly employment report will be released.

"The fact is the economy is in very good shape and the major point is to what extent are labour costs accelerating," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "The wage portion of the employment report holds that secret."

In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury rose 19/32, or $5.94 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield to 6.74 percent from 6.79 percent on Friday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Recent data have pointed to strong economic growth in the fourth quarter but just as importantly virtually no signs of inflation.
Two reports Monday showed consumers' incomes rose sharply as 1996 ended but that manufacturing was slowing.
The Commerce Department said incomes from wages, salaries and other sources rose 0.8 percent in December after rising 0.6 percent in November.

Separately, the National Association of Purchasing Management said its index of manufacturing fell to 52.0 in January from a revised 53.8 in December. A reading above 50 signals growth while one under that level points to contraction.
The reports pointed to steady growth without inflation.
In late New York trading, the dollar fetched 1.6400 German marks and 121.70 Japanese yen, up from 1.6387 marks and 121.43 yen Friday.
In commodities markets, coffee prices resumed their rise as worries about tight supplies ignited buying by speculators.
Coffee for March delivery rose 6.25 cents to close at 145.65 cents a pound at the Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange, just shy of the 16-month high of 147.80 cents set on Jan. 29.
March crude oil ended unchanged at $24.15 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange.

Overseas, London's leading FTSE 100 index finished just off the day's worst levels, down 18.0 points at 4,257.8. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average fell 244.06 points, or 1.33 percent, to 18,085.95.
